record.original_question: Is every compact space of weight ω1 homeomorphic to the remainder of a ψ-space, where a ψ-space is obtained from a maximal almost disjoint family of subsets of ω and the remainder is taken with respect to the Stone–Čech compactification of that ψ-space?

evidence.quote: Question 13. Is every compact space of weight ω1 homeomorphic to the remainder of a ψ-space?
A ψ-space is the usual kind of space obtained by taking a maximal almost disjoint family of subsets of ω and its remainder means with respect to its Stone-ˇCech compactiﬁcation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\omega$ denote the set of natural numbers. A family $\mathcal{A}$ of infinite subsets of $\omega$ is called almost disjoint if $A \cap B$ is finite for any two distinct $A, B \in \mathcal{A}$, and maximal almost disjoint (MAD) if it is maximal with respect to inclusion among such families. For a MAD family $\mathcal{A}$, the associated $\psi$-space (Isbell–Mrówka space) $\psi(\mathcal{A})$ has underlying set $\omega \cup \mathcal{A}$, where every point of $\omega$ is isolated, and a basic neighborhood of a point $A \in \mathcal{A}$ has the form $\{A\} \cup (A \setminus F)$ for some finite $F \subset \omega$. The space $\psi(\mathcal{A})$ is locally compact, Hausdorff, first countable, and (since $\mathcal{A}$ is maximal) pseudocompact. Let $\beta\psi(\mathcal{A})$ denote its Stone–Čech compactification, and define the remainder of $\psi(\mathcal{A})$ to be $\beta\psi(\mathcal{A}) \setminus \psi(\mathcal{A})$.

Question: Is every compact Hausdorff space of topological weight $\omega_1$ homeomorphic to the remainder $\beta\psi(\mathcal{A}) \setminus \psi(\mathcal{A})$ of some $\psi$-space arising from a maximal almost disjoint family $\mathcal{A} \subset [\omega]^\omega$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears to remain open. Subsequent work (e.g., Fox, "Extending the class of known Stone–Čech remainders for ψ-spaces", 2015) has progressively enlarged the class of compact spaces known to be realized as remainders of ψ-spaces (compact ordinals, compact metric spaces, certain compactifications, powers of compact metric spaces, etc.), but no complete characterization or affirmative answer for all compact spaces of weight ω₁ has been found, and no negative answer is reported.

status_evidence.title: Extending the class of known Stone–Čech remainders for ψ-spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Provides a class of spaces that can be realized as Stone–Čech remainders of ψ-spaces, including compact ordinals, compact metric spaces, compact separable first countable spaces, and more.
status_evidence.claim: The class of known remainders has been progressively extended but the question is not reported as fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Extending the Class of Known Stone-Čech Remainders for ψ-spaces — abstract (Keith Fox)
status_evidence.snippet: Abstract describing extensions of the class of compact spaces realizable as remainders of ψ-spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Work continues to expand which compact spaces are remainders of ψ-spaces, indicating the general weight-ω₁ question is still investigated.
